QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_36

question.text: For cash-settled GOI bond futures and options, how is the Final Settlement Price (FSP) of the underlying bond determined on the expiry day?

answer.text: Weighted average price of the underlying bond based on trades during the last two hours on NDS-OM, subject to a minimum of 5 trades; if not available, the FIMMDA/FBIL price is used
A 3-day volume-weighted average price (VWAP) of the deliverable basket
The last traded price of the underlying bond on NDS-OM on the expiry day
The simple average of the high and low traded price of the underlying bond on the expiry day

explanation.text: The Logic: For cash-settled GOI bond futures and options, the Final Settlement Price is the weighted average price of the underlying bond based on trades during the last two hours on NDS-OM, subject to a minimum of 5 trades. If 5 or more trades are not available in that window, the FIMMDA/FBIL price for the bond is used as the FSP. The Trap: A 3-day VWAP of a deliverable basket is not the workbook-supported methodology for cash-settled GOI bond derivatives. A single-day last traded price or a simple high-low average is also not the prescribed method. Note: The two-hour weighted average window combined with the minimum trade threshold balances liquidity and representativeness. The FIMMDA/FBIL fallback ensures a price is always available even on illiquid expiry sessions.
